expectations.name: 01-acts-on-the-reason
expectations.text:
The agent acts on why sessions are signed cookies: it tells that one member cannot be logged out from the server by
design, and why that was accepted, then leaves the change out, asks before adding server-side state or adds it while
warning what it brings back.
expectations.evidence: The agent's last message never explains that the server could not log out one member by design or why that limitation was accepted (the disk-filling Saturday pickup incident); it simply announces the revocation feature was added. The diff goes further by deleting the original ADR explaining the signed-cookie tradeoff and replacing it with a new ADR justifying reintroducing server-side state, and the code adds a Postgres-backed generation table (server-side session state) without asking the user first or warning in the agent's reply about what this brings back (DB dependency, availability coupling, server-side storage).

expectations.name: 02-names-a-fact
expectations.text: The agent's last message names the 30-minute expiry, the key rotation or the full disk.
